quotes.text: For subscriptions with `collection_method` set to `send_invoice`, Stripe emails the customer a link to the invoice with a configurable due date. For subscriptions without a trial, the initial subscription status is `active`, even if the first invoice is unpaid.
When a subscription becomes `active`, Stripe creates an active [entitlement](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/entitlements.md) for each feature associated with the subscribed product.
**Most recent invoice**: This is the default behavior. Stripe uses the most recent non-voided invoice. Other outstanding invoices don’t prevent the subscription from becoming `active`.
An invoice that Stripe marks uncollectible after ending payment retries remains outstanding. Stripe checks applicable invoices from the previous 37 months.
Smart Retries and custom retry rules don’t retry the initial payment while the subscription is `incomplete`.

old_evidence.text: When you create a subscription for a customer, this creates an active [entitlement](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/entitlements.md) for each feature associated with that product.

Stripe re-attempts payment using [Smart Retries](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/automatic-collection.md#smart-retries) or based on your custom [retry rules](https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/billing/automatic).
You can update the first invoice for a subscription if the [collection_method](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/object.md#subscription_object-collection_method) is `send_invoice`.

findings: The complete new capture at https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/overview is a substantive lifecycle revision. Initial `charge_automatically` invoices and the 23-hour incomplete window are scoped at new 31,39-43; `send_invoice` without a trial can start `active` with its first invoice unpaid at 33. The current source's unqualified 23-hour statement (source 21-23) overgeneralizes the automatic-collection case.

The new capture conditions active status on configurable most-recent-versus-all-invoices resolution (new 77-108,118,130-139). An applicable outstanding invoice is finalized, due and unsettled; the 37-month lookback and uncollectible-reason distinction are at 104-106. A paid PaymentIntent/invoice need not turn an existing `past_due` or `unpaid` subscription active when another governing invoice remains. The current source's matrix (source 38-44) and shorthand status rows (25-36) are incomplete for this setting.

Initial `incomplete` payment recovery requires collection/confirmation by the integration; Smart Retries and custom rules do not retry that initial payment (new 141-156). Later recurring failures have separate retry settings and final outcomes (new 160-164). The old capture's retry advice at old 149-155 appears in its generic payment-method recovery section and is unsafe to carry over as an initial-payment retry promise.

The new provisioning condition is subscription activation and active entitlements (new 47-51,180); `invoice.paid` plus status or entitlements confirmation is the documented gate in recovery/authentication paths (new 151-154,176-180). Delayed-confirmation methods can be active while PaymentIntent is processing and can remain active after later failure and voiding (new 122-125,137). Neither `active` nor `invoice.paid` alone proves every invoice was paid or every delayed payment finally succeeded.

The new raw distinguishes `trialing`, `active`, `incomplete`, `incomplete_expired`, `past_due`, `canceled`, `unpaid`, and `paused` at 75-88, with failed-payment settings and trial-end missing-method settings controlling some outcomes. Cancellation, Checkout incomplete-session update limits, and delayed confirmation are substantially retained at new 57,65-69,122-125 versus old 69,91-95,124. The removed first-invoice update subsection (old 71-77) remains historical captured evidence; omission is no proof of deprecation.

Root index 7 routes to Stripe index 606 and concept `wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md` at 792; the concept reciprocally links this source at 213. The dated concept statements at 16,18,20,60,80-85,175 need review because they present old payment behavior, universal 23-hour/async/provisioning shortcuts and entitlement timing without the new qualifications. No canonical page was edited.
substantive_changes: Collection-method split: 23-hour `incomplete` first-payment rule is explained for `charge_automatically`; `send_invoice` without trial can begin `active` with unpaid invoice (new 31-43 versus old 40-55).

Status resolution now has a default most-recent-non-voided-invoice option and an all-applicable-invoices option, with different reactivation and outstanding-invoice outcomes, delayed reevaluation, 37-month window, and uncollectible-reason distinctions (new 77-108 versus old 103-110).

Payment success matrix now conditions active on settlement of governing invoices; initial recovery does not use automatic retries, while recurring failure may use Smart Retries/custom rules (new 116-164 versus old 118-155).

Entitlements are described as active when the subscription becomes active, not simply on subscription creation; authentication flow now names `stripe.handleNextAction` and confirms subscription active or entitlements before provision (new 49,176-180 versus old 59,169-174).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The May 2026 capture's specific `default_incomplete`, `allow_incomplete`, and `error_if_incomplete` descriptions (old 29-38) remain dated evidence. The new overview only says `payment_behavior` can override a payment-method-dependent default (new 25); omission does not deprecate those values or establish a new universal default.

The May 2026 first-invoice update limits for `send_invoice`, `charge_automatically`, and schedules (old 71-77; source 50-54) remain attributed to that capture. Their omission from the November overview is not proof that update windows or schedule constraints ceased to apply.

The old capture's Stripe.js `stripe.ConfirmCardPayment` authentication example (old 169-174) is historical client-flow evidence. The November capture uses `stripe.handleNextAction` (new 176-180); the page comparison alone does not establish SDK-wide removal of the old method.
conflicts: Current source 23 and concept 18 describe a general first-invoice 23-hour rule; new 31-43 scope it to `charge_automatically` and distinguish `send_invoice` active-with-unpaid-invoice.

Current source 42 says succeeded/paid always maps to active; new 118,134 condition activation on governing invoices and can retain `past_due` or `unpaid` under all-invoices resolution. Concept 22/123-125 lacks this setting distinction.

Current source 48 and concept 20 say delayed methods skip incomplete and go active; new 124 says they can do so, and new 137 says PaymentIntent can still be processing. Preserve possibility rather than universal behavior.

Current source 58-60 and concept 60,80-85,175 imply invoice-paid, Checkout completion or subscription creation suffices for provisioning/entitlements; new 49,154,180 require activation or active entitlements in the stated flows. Concept 175's creation-timed entitlement assertion is directly contrary to new 49.

Current source 59 says `invoice.payment_failed` handles Smart Retry updates without distinguishing first versus recurring payment; new 156 excludes automatic retry while initially `incomplete`, whereas new 160-164 cover recurring-payment retries. Concept 16 also presents `default_incomplete` as a current universal recommendation absent from new 25.
unresolved_questions: Whether the May 2026 first-invoice editing constraints and named payment_behavior options remain current in their dedicated API/invoice guides is not resolved by omission in this overview capture.
The new overview names `stripe.handleNextAction` but does not establish version-wide support, deprecation or exclusivity relative to the older `stripe.ConfirmCardPayment` example.

The new overview's own generic confirmation wording at 39 and 139 must be read with its explicit status-resolution and delayed-confirmation qualifications at 77-108,118,124,137; a single webhook/status signal is not a universal payment-finality guarantee.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/overview, the November capture distinguishes `charge_automatically` first-payment `incomplete` and 23-hour expiry from `send_invoice` without a trial, which can begin `active` despite an unpaid first invoice (new 31-43; old 40-55). It adds invoice-dependent status resolution, separates initial collection from recurring retries, and ties provisioning to activated subscriptions or active entitlements (new 77-108,151-164,180). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-overview]] currently states a general 23-hour window, always-active success matrix, and older creation-timed entitlement framing (source 21-23,38-48; old 57-61). Customer, Subscription, Invoice, PaymentIntent and stored payment-method identities remain distinct (new 9-21,110-125).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/overview, the substantive changes are collection-method scope, configurable status resolution, conditional active status, initial-versus-recurring retry rules, and entitlement timing (new 31-49,77-108,118,151-164 versus old 40-59,103-124,149-155). Heading and link changes are presentational. [[source-stripe-subscriptions-overview]] should retain May 2026 payment_behavior options and first-invoice editing limits as dated evidence (old 29-38,71-77), since their omission is not deprecation. Reciprocal concept warnings should correct categorical async and Checkout provisioning claims; `active` can coexist with processing, later failed delayed payment, or other open invoices (new 80,122-125,137,180), so neither UI event nor payment-status row alone proves final settlement.
